title: Resolve an ordered role list and refuse to guess an unknown name
action: Per D2 (store 06e49368), widen the single resolver from one slot name to an ORDERED LIST of role names: walk the list, first name that resolves wins, and the caller's last entry is guaranteed to resolve because it falls back to the runtime's built-in default_models entry. THE CENTRAL FIX: models.rs:328 reads `let s = if CONFIGURABLE_SLOTS.contains(&slot) { slot } else { "generation" };` — it silently coerces ANY unrecognized name to generation and returns that model, while prepare.rs:1067 stamps tier_source:'cell' so the record asserts the cell chose it. Under an open role set that turns a typo (role: 'tset') into a wrong-model dispatch that completes clean with no red output. That coercion must go: an unconfigured name yields to the next entry and WARNS, and no path may resolve a name the config does not carry without warning. Retire CONFIGURABLE_SLOTS (:37) and MODEL_NORMALIZE_SLOTS (:40) as closed membership lists — any name present in models.<runtime> is legal. Leave the guard's struct-shaped config and its closed tier lists to mrs-3, and slot_for_kind to mrs-4.

truths: A configured custom role name resolves to its model
An unconfigured or misspelled name NEVER silently resolves a model: it warns and yields to the next list entry
The last entry of any list always resolves, so a walk cannot dead-end
An empty list and a one-entry list both behave as specified rather than panicking
A configured role is still obeyed exactly, per decision 72f3d6dd
The full suite is green, with every retargeted or deleted test named on the cap

trace.outcome: resolve_role walks an ordered role list; the unknown-name coercion to generation is gone and warns instead
deviations: Added packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/tests.rs to scope and reserved it under mrs-w2 — the cell requires retargeted tests be named. Retargeted 2 assertions in resolve_tier_covers_every_documented_slot_shape: resolve_tier(advisor) no longer coerces to generation/sonnet (now Budget), and the cli refusal names slot generation (the slot actually read) instead of review (the slot asked for). Added resolve_role_walks_the_list_and_refuses_to_guess_an_unknown_name. No test deleted.

MODEL_NORMALIZE_SLOTS deleted outright (nothing used it once normalize_models opened to every configured key). CONFIGURABLE_SLOTS kept, no longer a membership test — it survives as the default_models key list because prepare.rs still imports it; that sweep is mrs-4.

The stderr warning fires for a name absent from BOTH models.<runtime> and default_models (the typo case). A present-but-null slot yields silently: warning there would print on every dispatch of an unconfigured runtime, where every codex/opencode slot ships null by default.

The last-entry default_models floor is consulted ONLY for a key the table does not carry. An explicit null resolves to Budget: answering it with the built-in default resurrected the model the config had just cleared, and model_guard::cli_slot_and_empty_and_malformed_model_sets caught it red before this was fixed.

resolve_tier is kept as the single-name spelling of resolve_role rather than left beside it, so the fix reaches the model-guard and prepare.rs now instead of becoming dead code until mrs-3/mrs-4 sweep their call sites.
